newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan January trade surplus down 0.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan January trade surplus down 0.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan had a trade surplus of US$1.035 billion in January, down 0.6 percent from a surplus of US$1.041 billion in January 1996, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
January's exports were reported at US$10.326 billion, a decline of 3.4 percent from January 1996, while January imports were US$9.291 billion, down 3.7 percent year on year, the ministry said.

The January surplus was significantly larger than an average forecast of US$822 million compiled from Tuesday's poll Taiwan economists. That average forecast would have represented a 21.11 percent year-on-year decline in the January surplus.
The January export figure was quite close to the economists' average forecast of US$10.308 billion, while the import figure was somewhat farther from their average forecast of US$9.486 billion.
The finance ministry, in a brief summary, attributed the slight declines in January exports and imports to a relatively high comparative basis in January 1996.

The ministry noted that the export figure marked the third consecutive month in which exports had surpassed US$10 billion and said that January exports and imports both were at their highest level since February 1996.
"The actual performance in exports and imports is still good, despite the slight declines," the summary said.
The ministry said the outlook for Taiwan's foreign trade and the overall local economy appeared to be good.

"Looking to the future, with stable growth in the international economy and increasing local demand, the domestic economy is expected to recover gradually and our foreign trade is expected to maintain stable growth this year," it said.
In the Reuters poll, economists gave the same reason for expecting a downturn for exports and imports, saying trade was peaking in January 1996, skewing the year-on-year comparison.

The economists said further distortion of the figures was expected to result from the variable date of Taiwan's biggest holiday, the lunar new year, which fell on February 19 in 1996 but comes nearly two weeks earlier this year, on February 7.
The holiday usually lasts some five days, but manufacturers always take a longer rest, a factor that accentuates its impact on exports value in the month in which it falls, they said.

Trade balance 1,035.3 1,041.2 -0.6

January exports to the United States fell an annual 1.3 percent to $2.44 billion, accounting for 23.7 percent of the island's total exports and surpassing Hong Kong to become Taiwan's top export target in January, the ministry said.
Exports to Hong Kong were down a year-on-year 4.8 percent to $2.23 billion, accounting for 21.6 percent of the total.
Japan remained Taiwan's top single import source, accounting for $2.24 billion or 24.1 percnet of the total, followed by the United States at $1.95 billion and Europe at $1.64 billion.
Taiwan's January trade surplus with the United States was $490 million, up a scant 0.3 percent from January 1996.
The January surplus with Hong Kong decreased 4.8 percent to $2.04 billion.
The surplus with Europe was at $50 million, compared with a January 1996 deficit of $100 million.
Taiwan's trade deficit with Japan was down 14.6 percent at $1.16 billion.
-- Taipei Newsroom (886-2-5080815)
